issues.title: reporting in request mode
issues.author: gwendalsimon
issues.body:
The draft says that "_Since Request mode is tied to HTTP requests, which are not present in MOQT, this specification constrains CMCD usage to those options offered in Event Mode. Request mode MUST NOT be used._' 

It could be possible to declare a CMCD track that _depends_ on a given track. And then the Subscriber could report a CMCD data object related to the Location of that track.

In the catalog, it would be something like
{
  "version": "1",
  "generatedAt": 1746104606044,
  "tracks": [
    {
      "name": "video",
      "namespace": "broadcast.example.com/live/stream1",
      "packaging": "loc",
      "isLive": true,
      "targetLatency": 2000,
      "role": "video",
      "renderGroup": 1,
      "codec": "av01.0.08M.10.0.110.09",
      "width": 1920,
      "height": 1080,
      "framerate": 30,
      "bitrate": 1500000
    },
  ],
  "publishTracks": [
     {
      "namespace": "example.com/collection/cmcd/report",
      "name": "%player-id%",
      "packaging": "eventtimeline",
      "eventType": "urn:cta:cmcd:2026",
      **"depends": "video"**
      "cmcdConfig" : {
         **"events": ["L"],**
         "enabledKeys": ["sid","bl","br","bs","ltc","msd","mtp"]
     }
    ]
}

And then the CMCD track record would be 
{
        **"L": (12,0),**
        "data": {
            "sid":"6e2fb550-c457-11e9-bb97-0800200c9a66",
            "bl": 4068,
            "br": "(5000;v 320;a)",
            "bsd": 321,
            "e":"t",
            "sta": "p",
            "v": 2
        }
}

comments.author: t0ms
comments.body:
From the transport-stream side, +1 to tying a report to a track. The failures we measured that
nothing else detects are partial: one elementary stream stops while the others, and the mux's own
timing, carry on. A report that can name the track it is about would serve CMCD's per-type values and
any container-health event type alike.

(Written by Claude Opus 5.5)

issues.title: Container-level health beside CMCD: transport-stream receivers
issues.author: t0ms
issues.body:
We carry broadcast MPEG-TS over MoQ for contribution and primary distribution, where the receivers are
gateways and IRDs rather than adaptive-bitrate players. The draft's mechanism is what that use needs:
the catalog tells the receiver where to publish its reports, and a token scopes it. We have exercised
the authorization half on one implementation: one token carrying a subscribe scope for the media and
an independent publish scope for a feedback namespace, each honoured on its own prefix and refused on
the other's, with a neighbouring tenant's namespace refused
([T39](https://github.com/tdrapier-wbd/moq-mpegts-paper/blob/main/lab/test-39-cross-boundary-observability.md),
Part C).

The vocabulary is the gap. An operator receiving a transport stream needs TR 101 290-class counters and
per-elementary-stream liveness, and the second matters more: a 57.22 s hole in a broadcast mux's video
passed the whole TR 101 290 priority-1 set with zero continuity errors, and only counting access units
per stream caught every fault arm we injected
([T24](https://github.com/tdrapier-wbd/moq-mpegts-paper/blob/main/lab/test-24-partial-media-plane-stall.md)).
CMCD has no keys for either. The draft does allow CMCD's custom event (`ce`, named by `cen`), which
could name a fault such as a silent stream, but CTA-5004-B carries a custom event's value in a custom
key, and since `enabledKeys` takes only the keys §3 lists, custom keys, and with them the value, are
not available as written.

Two ways to leave room, and we lean to the second:

1. Allow custom CMCD keys (hyphen-prefixed, as CTA-5004-B requires) in `enabledKeys`, under the same
   rate guidance.
2. Say that container- or packaging-specific health belongs in its own Event Timeline type in a
   separate `publishTracks` entry, which a catalog can request from the same receiver beside a CMCD
   track. CMCD stays a player vocabulary, and a transport-stream health type can be defined with the
   MPEG-TS packaging work.

Either way, a fault of this kind is per track, which is also the point of #3.

(Written by Claude Opus 5.5)
